threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think every café is overpriced until you find that tucked-away spot with the best flat white. Welcome to the hunt!
Last night on the 196, a bloke serenaded us with a ukulele while the driver pretended to be unimpressed. Classic Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the old Turkish baker remembers everyone's name and asks about their kids. That's when it hit me; this place isn't just a stop, it's home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you hear a techno rave while waiting for a bus. It's like the city's heartbeat has its own soundtrack.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their ability to seamlessly dodge the persistent BART delays while juggling burritos on their way to the park.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 out-dancing everyone during a packed commute. Muni's the stage; you just never know who's dropping a performance!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves mojitos. In Gràcia, it’s definitely more about vermut and tapas—no fancy cocktails needed.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the metro map—always staring at it like it’s a magic puzzle. Longtime locals know the shortcuts.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always tell the newbies by how they can't differentiate a 'Boris bike' from a Santander cycle. We see you, it's cute.
Last night on the 50, a passenger tried to convince the driver to play his mixtape. Never seen someone so determined to get their tunes heard at 3 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy casually repairing his bike while a busker played tango near the canal, I knew this place was special.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery. Late-night snacks and local art collide in the most unexpected ways.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART during rush hour after a loud bang; the panic's palpable but they’re already strategizing their next move.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy juggling on the 47. One hand had a coffee, the other a half-eaten burrito. Only in SF do we multi-task like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the bars, but the real gem is the local markets where the true rhythm of life beats.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they struggle to open the trash bins; locals have mastered the foot pedal technique long ago.
